narrative: Material PL1__M4AA1B3D exhibits smooth, normally distributed demand (mean 1,608 units/day, CV 16.44%) with no detectable trend, making it well-suited to a continuous-review (R,Q) replenishment policy. Lead times average 1.25 days but are highly unstable (CV 75.13%), contributing 96.3% of total demand-uncertainty variance and requiring a safety stock of 2,530 units to meet the 95% service level. The current SAP policy effectively orders at MOQ (986 units), generating excessive replenishment frequency and ordering costs; the optimised EOQ of 28,738 units (capped at 23,505 units by storage constraints) consolidates replenishments to ~17 per year, cutting total annual inventory costs by 95.2% from $20,485 to $978. Storage expansion is recommended to unlock the full unconstrained EOQ benefit.
warnings: Storage constraint active: reduced order quantity from 28738 to 23505

research_insights.selected_model: (R,Q) continuous-review with EOQ and safety stock
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, normally distributed demand (CV=16.44%) with 100% non-zero fraction supports a continuous-review (R,Q) policy. The unstable lead time (CV=75.13%) necessitates a statistically derived safety stock using the combined demand-lead-time variance formula rather than a fixed safety lead time.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity caps the order quantity at 23,505 units (vs. unconstrained EOQ of 28,738). This increases annual ordering frequency from ~14 to ~17 orders/year and raises ordering cost from the theoretical minimum. A storage expansion of ~3,233 units would eliminate the constraint.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Storage expansion recommended to achieve full EOQ savings. MOQ (986) is well below the order quantity and poses no infeasibility conflict.
